page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 16 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is driven by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores with a single thread per core. This instance features shared CPU allocation and runs on the KVM hypervisor. It integrates two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Notably, this server does not include local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in single-core and multi-core operations. The server achieves top-10% placement in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU tests. Memory performance is strong, with large-block read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 25%. In LLM inference tests, the system demonstrates top-tier efficiency for small models in both prompt processing and text generation, while maintaining strong to average performance on larger 7B and 70B parameter models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density, balancing a substantial memory footprint of 12.0 GB per core with dual enterprise-grade GPUs. The lack of bundled local storage represents a tradeoff, shifting storage costs to external network volumes. This hardware profile is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, including machine learning inference, data science tasks, image processing, and parallel computing workloads that leverage the Ada Lovelace architecture.
